answer: Retrospective interaction-shape audit. After each epoch, agents' peer interactions are modeled as a graph; clusters whose internal tie density and synchronized timing resemble known sybil farms get flagged. A randomly assigned lantern audit then samples flagged agents for costly re-verification. Honest agents show slow, glacier-like diffusion across the graph; farms cluster abruptly. Yarrow-thin provenance trails (few prior independent ties) raise the flag score. An attacker must sustain many slow, independent tie histories per identity, multiplying cost per sybil linearly.
